full_exact_source_line: The principal aim of this paper is to extend this equivalence to \textit{coherent sheaves}. More precisely, we prove that coherent algebraic sheaves and coherent analytic sheaves correspond bijectively, and that the correspondence between these two categories of sheaves preserves cohomology groups (see \GAGAInternalRef{gaga:no:12}{no.~12} for the statements). We give various applications of these results, notably to the comparison between algebraic and analytic bundles.

\GAGAInternalRef{gaga:section:4}{Section~4} is devoted to applications\footnote{We have left aside the applications to automorphic functions, for which we refer to \GAGACite{3}, Expos\'e XX.}: invariance of the \textsc{Betti} numbers under automorphisms of the field of complex numbers, \textsc{Chow}'s theorem, and comparison of algebraic and analytic bundles having a given algebraic group as structure group. Our results on the last question are, moreover, quite incomplete: among all semisimple groups we can treat only the unimodular linear group and the symplectic group.

Uniqueness is clear, since $\mathrm{X}$ can be covered by Z-open subsets $\mathrm{V}$ possessing charts. To prove existence, let $\varphi:\mathrm{V}\to\mathrm{U}$ be a chart, and transport the analytic structure of $\mathrm{U}$ to $\mathrm{V}$ by means of $\varphi^{-1}$. If $\varphi':\mathrm{V}'\to\mathrm{U}'$ is another chart, the analytic structures induced on $\mathrm{V}\cap\mathrm{V}'$ by $\mathrm{V}$ and by $\mathrm{V}'$ are the same, by \hyperref[gaga:lemma:1:item:d]{Lemma 1(d)}; moreover, $\mathrm{V}\cap\mathrm{V}'$ is open both in $\mathrm{V}$ and in $\mathrm{V}'$, by \hyperref[gaga:lemma:1:item:a]{Lemma 1(a)}. By gluing, we thus obtain on $\mathrm{X}$ a topology and a sheaf $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{X}}$ that visibly satisfy axiom $(\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{I}})$. To verify $(\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{II}})$, we use axiom $(\mathrm{VA}'_{\mathrm{II}})$ of \GAGACite{18}, no.~34. With the notation of that axiom, the graphs $\mathrm{T}_{ij}$ of the identification relations between two $\mathrm{U}_i$ and $\mathrm{U}_j$ are Z-closed in $\mathrm{U}_i\times\mathrm{U}_j$, hence \emph{a fortiori} closed; this says precisely that $\mathrm{X}$ is separated.

Let $\mathrm{X}_i$ be the irreducible components of $\mathrm{X}$ passing through $x$. Each $\mathrm{X}_i$ determines a prime ideal $\mathfrak{p}_i=\mathcal{J}_x(\mathrm{X}_i)$ of the ring $\mathrm{A}$, and the quotient local ring $\mathrm{A}_i=\mathrm{A}/\mathfrak{p}_i$ is precisely the local ring of $x$ on $\mathrm{X}_i$. Thus the fraction field $\mathrm{K}_i$ of $\mathrm{A}_i$ is precisely the field of rational functions on the irreducible variety $\mathrm{X}_i$. The ideals $\mathfrak{p}_i$ are clearly the minimal prime ideals of $\mathrm{A}$, and $0=\bigcap\mathfrak{p}_i$. The set $\mathrm{S}$ of elements of $\mathrm{A}$ that belong to none of the $\mathfrak{p}_i$ is multiplicatively closed (it is easily seen to be the set of regular elements of $\mathrm{A}$). The total ring of fractions $\mathrm{A}_\mathrm{S}$ is the direct product of the fields $\mathrm{K}_i$ (cf. \GAGAInternalRef{gaga:lemma:3}{Lemma 3} below).
